ceiling_directive: Upgrade the ambiguity frontier to a singleton-domain theorem by proving partition uniqueness for arbitrary incomparable crossings and strict refinements with external fine parents over the full innovation-atomic GANM class.
improvement_directive: Prove a general nondescendant-conditioning lemma that survives conditioning through correlated competing innovations, together with a quotient lemma eliminating external fine-parent terms. Use them to strengthen the recovery theorem from a partial-function identified set to uniqueness of the admissible partition.
critique: Population identification of the generating causal-unit partition is not proved: the domain of the recovery map may contain multiple incomparable or refinement-related partitions. The partial-function conclusion identifies only the DAG conditional on a supplied admissible partition, and that graph uniqueness is inherited from the cited fixed-partition theorem. The new cross-partition results exclude only unequal empty-DAG factorizations, one three-coordinate crossed single-edge pattern, and coarse-root refinements whose fine blocks have no external parents; arbitrary crossings and externally parented refinements remain open. The framing accurately disclaims global uniqueness and finite certification, so there is no stale prose over-claim, but the delivered result is a narrow ambiguity frontier rather than the requested identification theorem.
